name: familiar
description: Familiar names (#433, #3032): the geometry, light, camera, material and fog words agents know from web 3D libraries, with their parameter names and defaults, each a recipe over scene3d's trusted builders and kinds with its conversion stated. A word or value with no mapping is refused, never guessed.

BoxGeometry.conversion: its parameters by name; angles in degrees; Object3D's rotation (XYZ) through the rotation matrix to ours (Rz·Ry·Rx), its pivot to our position plus that pivot

MeshStandardMaterial.conversion: Color sRGB to linear base_color; roughness kept; metalness to metallic

PointLight.conversion: power = 4π × intensity (cd), kept in lumens; Color sRGB to linear; decay 2 only

SpotLight.conversion: power × 4 (the library's spot counts π × cd, ours 4π × cd); angle the outer half angle; penumbra to inner

PerspectiveCamera.conversion: vertical fov to ours across the wider side, 2·atan(tan(fov/2)·aspect) when aspect ≥ 1; local −Z forward to our target

DirectionalLight.conversion: illuminance = intensity, kept in lux: the library lights a surface that faces the light with color × intensity as its irradiance; Color sRGB to linear; it shines from position, (0, 1, 0) unwritten, toward target

AmbientLight.conversion: ambient_top = ambient_low = color × intensity ÷ π: the library's intensity is an irradiance in lux, ours the radiance a white surface reflects; Color sRGB to linear; one sky a document, the first sky@1 it holds

HemisphereLight.conversion: ambient_top = skyColor × intensity ÷ π and ambient_low = groundColor × intensity ÷ π, mixed by the normal's height as the library mixes them; Colors sRGB to linear; position straight up only, the library's default; one sky a document, the first sky@1 it holds

RectAreaLight.conversion: power = π × intensity × width × height: the library's intensity is the face's luminance in cd/m², ours the lumens the face sends out; size [width, height] in metres; Color sRGB to linear; it shines along its local −Z, its rotation (XYZ) through the rotation matrix to ours (Rz·Ry·Rx)

OrthographicCamera.conversion: view_width = right − left; the frustum's centre, ((left + right) ÷ 2, (top + bottom) ÷ 2), moves the position and target in the view's plane; the view's height follows the frame, as the library's does when the frustum's aspect is the frame's; local −Z forward to our target

MeshBasicMaterial.conversion: unlit: true, so it draws its color whatever lights it; Color sRGB to linear base_color

MeshLambertMaterial.conversion: specular_level 0, so it reflects by its diffuse lobe alone; Color sRGB to linear base_color; emissive × emissiveIntensity to emission × emission_strength

MeshPhysicalMaterial.conversion: color, roughness, metalness to metallic and emissive as MeshStandardMaterial's; clearcoat to coat; sheen to sheen.weight; thickness and attenuation to absorption, an attenuationDistance of 0 for the library's Infinity; iridescenceThicknessRange's upper end to the film's thickness in nm; anisotropyRotation in degrees; specularIntensity ÷ 2 to specular_level; Colors sRGB to linear

FogExp2.conversion: fog_density = density in 1/m under fog_curve exp2, a share of 1 − exp(−(density × d)²) in both; ours reads d from the eye and mixes in linear light, the library reads depth along the view axis and mixes the encoded picture; Color sRGB to linear; one sky a document, the first sky@1 it holds
